newsitem.title: USA: U.S. processor recalls 1.2 mln pounds of hamburger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. processor recalls 1.2 mln pounds of hamburger.

text.p: Arkansas meat processor Hudson Foods Inc. is recalling 1.2 million pounds of frozen hamburger nationwide due to possible contamination with a deadly strain of the E. coli bacteria, Agriculture Department officials said Friday.

The new recall by the Arkansas-based firm was in addition to a voluntary recall of some of its hamburger patties earlier this week after the meat was linked to 16 cases of human illness in Colorado in July.
The department also said it was launching an investigation into why it took so long for the full scope of the possible contamination at Hudson Foods to be known.
It warned consumers who have bought Hudson Farms frozen ground beef patties since June 4 to return any unused portion to where it was purchased.
The frozen patties were distributed nationwide in retail grocery stores, wholesale stores and in some restaurants.
The 1.2 million pounds of hamburger involved in the recall were processed at the firm's Columbus, Nebraska, facility on June 4, 5 and 9, the department said.
"We are continuing to examine the records to determine if there is any further product implicated," said Tom Billy, administrator of the department's Food Safety and Inspection Service.
The Agriculture Department initially announced this week that Hudson Foods was recalling 20,000 pounds of frozen patties distributed to stores and another 20,000 pounds distributed to restaurants.
"USDA is conducting a thorough investigation at the plant to ensure no unsafe product is being allowed to go into commerce," U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said.

The inquiry includes examining records at the Columbus, Nebraska plant to determine why there was a dely "in the full report of the production records," USDA Undersecretary for Food Safety Catherine Woteki said.
Once that review is complete, "USDA will take appropriate corrective action," she said.
